hyps.why: Replacing a removed edge with conv3x3 restores connectivity, so the gain is larger than when replacing an existing op.
Edge 5 is the only way for node 2 to reach the output, so filling it from none gives a large gain.
Replacing none with a strong conv gains more than replacing an op that already carries signal.
Adding a direct input-to-output shortcut where none exists improves gradient flow more than swapping one op for another.
Replacing none with conv3x3 adds a new learnable path and gains more than replacing an existing op.
Replacing none with conv3x3 adds depth and capacity, so the gain is larger than when replacing another op.
Removing an existing skip shortcut is more harmful than removing a weaker op such as avg_pool.
Replacing a useful skip shortcut with conv gains less than replacing none or a pool.
With edge 4 already removed, one of node 1's routes to the output is gone, so removing edge 0 costs less.
Removing a strong conv edge costs far more than removing a weak op such as avg_pool.
